project_subtitle: Predicting life expectancy from WHO health-system indicators using local heavy benchmarks and an optional TabPFN reference
analytical_question: Can public health indicators from WHO explain observable variation and predict differences in life expectancy across countries?

chapters.title: The data foundation
chapters.description: WHO indicators are broad, historical and unevenly complete across countries and years.

chapters.title: The health-system signals
chapters.description: Mortality, immunization, expenditure and data-quality signals structure the predictive layer.

chapters.title: The prediction layer
chapters.description: A heavy local benchmark identifies the strongest predictive model, while TabPFN remains an optional external reference.

chapters.title: Residual intelligence
chapters.description: Outliers reveal countries performing better or worse than expected given the available signals.
